newsitem.title: USA: DeBakey sees rapid recovery for Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: DeBakey sees rapid recovery for Yeltsin.

text.p: Noted heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said on Wednesday that he expected a quick recovery by Russian President Boris Yeltsin from what he said was likely a case of the flu.

"I expect him to be all right, and I would say that in a matter of three days to a week you're going to see improvement and (he'll) probably leave the hospital," DeBakey said in an interview on CNN. Yeltsin, who had major heart surgery on November 5, was taken to hospital in Moscow on Wednesday for what was described as a case of pneumonia.
DeBakey said he had talked to the doctor treating Yeltsin earlier on Wednesday and the doctor had advised the president to return to the hospital after detecting early signs of pneumonia.

DeBakey, who served as a consultant when Yeltsin underwent quintuple bypass surgery, said Russian doctors had found "a spot of pneumonitis" in one of Yeltsin's lungs, but that it had been caught before it could develop into a full-blown case of pneumonia.

"It sounds to me like what he has is the flu. Apparently, there's quite a bit of it going around in Moscow. Even some members of the family in the Kremlin have it," he said. He added that Yeltsin, 65, was being treated with antibiotics.

DeBakey said the illness "has nothing to do with the heart operation. In fact, he's really better off having the flu now after the operation than if he had the flu before...because his heart is functioning virtually normally now.
